headline: But Mattel doesn't have much on the side of kids.
subheadline: 'Frozen', the animated success of Disney, has been a weapon of double-edged sword for Mattel. The company owns the primary license for the toy of the movie and sells versions of dolls of Elsa and Anna. But there are other items related to 'Frozen'. Moreover, licensed products are less profitable due to royalty payments.

headline: To make matters worse: Hasbro beat out Mattel at last year’s bidding process for Disney Princesses and ‘Frozen’ and will take possession of those properties in 2016.

The broader industry of toys has been depressed for years, affected by changes in how children play. Now even elementary school-aged children have smartphones. Mobile games like Angry Birds and Candy Crush compete against extensive product ranges (from plush toys to board games).
But Mattel hasn’t seen significant benefits from the explosion of apps.
